title: People’s Liberation Army Air Force Aircraft that Flew Through Singapore’s Flight Information Region on 31 May 2021
what_it_is: People’s Liberation Army Air Force Aircraft that Flew Through Singapore’s Flight Information Region on 31 May 2021

sections.label: PLAAF aircraft through Singapore FIR
sections.summary: Members asked the Minister for Defence about 16 PLAAF aircraft that flew through Singapore's Flight Information Region on 31 May 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence regarding the 16 People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) aircraft that flew through Singapore’s Flight Information Region (FIR) on 31 May 2021 (a) whether the RSAF tracked the flight of these aircraft; (b) whether the RSAF was successful in establishing communications with them; (c) how many of such unannounced entries into Singapore's FIR by PLAAF aircraft have taken place in the past year; and (d) what are the plans to ensure the safety of flights to and from Singapore should tensions among rival claimants of islands in the South China Sea escalate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) what is the Government's situational assessment regarding the flight of 16 People’s Liberation Army Air Force aircraft that passed through Singapore’s Flight Information Region on 31 May 2021 over waters which are disputed by China and Malaysia; and (b) whether plans are in place to ensure the security and safety of flights to and from Singapore should tensions among rival claimants escalate in the airspace over the South China Sea.

sections.label: CAAS and PLAAF flight plans
sections.summary: CAAS received no flight plans from the PLAAF and did not communicate with the PLAAF or its aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In the incident referred to in the Members’ questions, CAAS did not receive any flight plans from the PLAAF, nor did it communicate with the PLAAF or any of its aircraft.

sections.label: RSAF responses to incidents
sections.summary: The RSAF responds to more than 350 such incidents each year, and the specific incident was not deemed such a threat.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: On average, each year, the RSAF responds to more than 350 such incidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The specific incident referred to by the two Members in their questions was not deemed to be such a threat.

sections.label: Detection aspects and 350 incidents
sections.summary: Aspects detected include movement and filed flight plans, and the 350 incidents are unrelated to the Members' questions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And there are a number of aspects that we would detect, whether it is movement, whether, indeed, flight plans have been filed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I have mentioned 350 such incidents and let me again emphasise, these 350 incidents have got nothing to do with the questions that the two Members have asked because they have framed their questions in a way that can actually give rise to misunderstanding and misinterpretations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: These 350 incidents that we have had, many of which RSAF had actually to mobilise.

sections.label: Not uniform, not majority
sections.summary: The answer is that it is not uniform and is not the majority.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The answer is it is not uniform and, in fact, it is not the majority.
